patient_diversity.note: 18 real synthetic patients plus the intentional invalid-patient sentinel ID used by the 2 invalid_patient cases.

data_source: Synthea synthetic FHIR R4 fixtures included with MEVA (data/synthetic/synthea/patient-01.json through patient-18.json), all from the official synthetichealth/synthea-sample-data repository. See docs/synthetic-data.md for the full source mapping. No real patient data is used anywhere in this dataset.
description: Stage 7B.5's comparison-ready benchmark suite: 15 additional official Synthea synthetic patients were added (18 total, up from 3) specifically to give this dataset enough patient diversity for meaningful multi-model comparison later. 4 cases (allergy-06, allergy-07, medication-07, condition-06) are 'multi_fact' regression cases that directly exercise the new attribute-level evidence/claim/verification support added in Stage 7B.5 — the same kind of case (an allergy's criticality and clinical status) that was previously and incorrectly scored UNSUPPORTED in the v0.2 benchmark. verifier-challenge-04 is a new attribute-level VERIFIER_CHALLENGE case proving MEVA's verifier catches a false attribute claim (wrong criticality) deterministically.
limitations: 56 cases across 18 synthetic patients are an engineering benchmark sample, not sufficient for clinical validation or statistical claims about model reliability.
Only one patient (patient-03) has any recorded allergies in the available Synthea fixture data, so all 8 allergy cases necessarily involve that one patient.

Attribute-level verification (Stage 7B.5) currently covers only allergy.criticality, allergy.clinical_status, medication.status, medication.intent, and condition.clinical_status/onset — fields already present in MEVA's existing tool output. It does not attempt general medical attribute extraction.
Tool over-calling and duplicate tool calls are measured but not penalized in pass/fail scoring.

Wrong-category structured claims from the model (e.g. labeling an allergy claim as category='patient') are never auto-corrected by MEVA — they remain a genuine, visible model failure rather than being silently repaired for a better score.
